title: Quality-bucket adjudication & rerank eval protocol (2026)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines the nearline protocol for pairwise label collection, adjudication, and conversion to graded relevance for NDCG calculations across reranking onboarding evaluations. Goal is to produce stable, explainable slices and statistical tests we can run automatically during model onboarding/regression checks.

Scope and prerequisites:
- Applies to reranking evaluation runs for hosted/dedicated/private model onboarding (candidate lists from search, assistant retrieval, or hybrid rerankers).
- Assumes candidate pools are pre-filtered to top-K (generally K=100) by a coarse retrieval step.
- Pairwise labels are collected per query-candidate pair comparisons sampled from pairwise pools (pooling strategy described below).

Key principles (informal):
- Preserve annotator signal: prefer inference techniques that use the pairwise votes (BT / Plackett-Luce) instead of naive majority-win heuristics when sample size per query is sufficient.
- Make slices actionable: slice definitions should map back to potential model/prompt/config levers.
- Keep adjudication light but traceable: minimize escalations by clearer label schema and simple adjudicator rules.

Sampling & pooling strategy:
- Goal sample: ~10k unique queries per run with stratification across traffic source, locale, and vertical.
- For each query, create a pairwise pool using 2-stage pooling:
  1) top-10 deterministic candidates (from model under test or baseline) always included;
  2) add 40 randomly sampled candidates from top-100 retrieval set (pool size ~= 50).
- Pairwise pairs: sample M pairs per query (M=25 default). If pool size small, sample all unique unordered pairs up to M.
- Rationale: balance coverage (diverse choices) with annotation cost.

Label schema (3-level preference):
- LEFT: left candidate is preferred over right (label = 1)
- EQUAL / TIE: annotator sees no meaningful difference (label = 0)
- RIGHT: right candidate preferred over left (label = -1)
- Additional annotation fields (optional): reason_code (quality, hallucination, factuality, format, relevance), comment (free text).
- We recommend 3 annotators per pair. Resolve with simple majority (2/3). If all three disagree (all different votes), escalate to adjudicator.

Adjudication procedure (shown for ambiguous triples):
- First-tier: automated majority resolution. Record annotator ids + time.
- Second-tier: adjudicator (senior annotator) reviews pair with full context (query, candidates, snippets, model metadata). Adjudicator picks from LEFT/EQUAL/RIGHT and must add a short reason_code.
- Logging: store pre-adjudication votes, final adjudicated label, adjudicator id, and free-text note.
- Adjudication SLA: target <= 48 hours for escalations for onboarding runs.

From pairwise preferences to graded relevance (recommended approaches):
- Short runs / low budget (safe/simple): wins-based score. For each query and candidate: wins = count of pairwise wins; total_comparisons = number of times candidate appeared; raw_score = wins/total_comparisons; map raw_score to graded relevance using thresholds: r>=0.75 -> 3, 0.5<=r<0.75 -> 2, 0.25<=r<0.5 -> 1, r<0.25 -> 0. Notes: fast, deterministic, interpretable but ignores transitive consistency.
- Primary recommended (statistically principled): Bradley-Terry (BT) / pairwise logistic model.
  - Fit BT per query across candidates (regularize globally to avoid degenerate estimates for low-data queries).
  - Convert BT latent ability theta_i to relevance using monotonic mapping to integer grades (e.g., quantile-based cutpoints tuned on validation set).
  - Advantage: handles transitivity and partial comparisons, provides uncertainty estimates for candidate scores.
- Plackett-Luce variant: use when full listwise permutations are available (rare for sampled pairs).

Edge cases and tie handling:
- If candidate never appears in any annotated pair for a query, mark as unjudged and exclude from NDCG calculation for that query (drop or treat as 0 depending on upstream agreement). Default: treat as unjudged and exclude that candidate from DCG computation but keep query if at least one judged candidate exists.
- When using wins-based binning, ties (EQUAL) count as 0.5 win for both sides when computing wins fraction. Document this choice in run metadata.

NDCG computation details (implementation notes):
- Use graded relevance per candidate (integers 0..G), DCG@k = sum_{i=1..k} (2^{rel_i}-1) / log2(i+1).
- Use ideal DCG computed on the graded relevance ranking (ties resolved by sorting candidates by descending aggregate score and then by candidate id for deterministic tie-break).
- Default cutoff: k=10 and k=100 reported. Report both micro-averaged and query-weighted (macro) NDCG.
- Missing graded relevance for top-k candidates: if a top-k candidate is unjudged and unresolvable, remove candidate from both system ranking and ideal list when computing DCG for that query (effectively reduce k for that query). Clearly record effective k per query.

Statistical tests and CI:
- Bootstrap by queries (not by pairs) to compute 95% CI for NDCG deltas: 1000 bootstrap samples recommended.
- Significance rule for regression alert: |delta_NDCG| >= 0.005 and p-value < 0.05 after bootstrap (two-sided). For high-sensitivity verticals (e.g., finance/healthcare) use delta threshold 0.0025.
- When comparing two systems, run paired bootstrap across queries to compute delta distribution. Also compute effect size (Cohen's d on per-query NDCG).

Per-slice analysis (operational slices we care about):
- Cold_start_queries: queries with no prior successful clicks in last 90 days (expect higher variance).
- Ambiguous_intent: queries with >=2 equally plausible intents (identified by intent classifier score spread).
- Short_query: length <=3 tokens.
- Long_query: length >=10 tokens or complex instruction-like inputs.
- Shopping_vertical: candidate doc type == product_catalog.
- Safety_sensitive: queries flagged by safety classifier (manual review required).
- For each slice report: N (queries), mean NDCG@10, delta vs baseline, bootstrap CI, top failure reasons (from reason_code aggregation).

Quality bucket definitions (for triage):
- Good: NDCG@10 > 0.85 and <5% of queries with catastrophic failures (reason_code==hallucination/factuality).
- Watch: 0.7 <= NDCG@10 <= 0.85 or 5-15% catastrophic failures.
- Needs_attention: NDCG@10 < 0.7 or >15% catastrophic failures.
- These buckets are guidance for SRE/product leads when routing follow-up investigations.

Operational checklist (pre-run):
- Confirm baseline model and candidate retrieval seed.
- Export top-100 candidate pools and sample pairwise pairs for annotation.
- Ensure annotation UI supports left/right/tie + reason_code + comment.
- Kick off 3 annotators per pair, monitor inter-rater agreement (Kripp alpha target >= 0.55 for overall dataset).
- Validate that adjudications < 6% of total pairs (otherwise refine schema).

Data storage and artifact schema (short):
- raw_pairs.csv: columns [query_id, left_id, right_id, left_text, right_text, annotator_id, vote, timestamp, reason_code, comment]
- adjudicated_pairs.csv: [query_id, left_id, right_id, final_vote, adjudicator_id, adjud_note]
- graded_relevance.jsonl: one row per (query_id, candidate_id, grade) plus metadata: method (BT/wins), run_id, mapping_cutpoints
- ndcg_run_summary.json: metrics per-query and per-slice plus CI and artifact links

Example quick code (pseudocode) for wins-based conversion:
- For q in queries:
    For c in candidates_for(q):
       wins[c] = number of pairs where c was preferred + 0.5 * number of ties
       total[c] = number of times c was in an annotated pair
       raw[c] = wins[c] / total[c] (if total[c]==0 -> mark unjudged)
    Map raw to grade: if raw>=0.75 -> 3; elif raw>=0.5 ->2; elif raw>=0.25 ->1; else 0

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate BT regularization hyperprior across verticals (how much shared strength among candidates should we allow).
- Should we impute graded relevance for unjudged top-k candidates using retrieval score? Pros/cons documented but needs A/B.
- Explore active sampling to prioritize informative pairs (uncertainty sampling) to reduce annotation cost by ~30%.

Appendix: examples for annotators (short):
- Q: "best noise cancelling headphones under $200"
  L: "Brand X ANC headphone review (2023)" ; R: "Top 10 headphones buyer's guide" -> Prefer R (more comprehensive shopping guide)
- Q: "how to reset my router"
  L: "reset using web interface steps" ; R: "factory reset via hardware button" -> Label depends on intent; if user asked for factory reset, prefer R; when unclear, mark reason_code=ambiguous and adjudicate.

Footnotes: This is a working operational protocol; expect iterations as we run 1-2 onboarding cycles and measure annotation costs vs. fidelity.
